# sources/test-tools/syzkaller/pkg/report/testdata/linux/report/479

Purpose: Linux reporter parse fixture for syzkaller. It encodes the expected parsed title `BUG: unable to handle kernel paging request in corrupted`, expected type `MEMORY_SAFETY_BUG`, alternate titles `bad-access in corrupted`, corrupted flag `Y`, and panicked flag `Y`. The source is a static kernel-console transcript, not executable test code; its job is to pin how the Linux reporter recognizes corrupted-list page faults in nf_tables flowtable path. It has no explicit REPORT block, so the parser derives the report from the console transcript and expected headers.

Important APIs, types, and functions: this file is consumed by `pkg/report/report_test.go` through `testParseImpl`, `Reporter.ContainsCrash`, `Reporter.Parse`, and `Reporter.ParseFrom`. It exercises Linux reporter pattern tables and title extraction in `linux.go`, generic report shaping in `report.go`, and crash-type mapping through `pkg/report/crash.TitleToType`. Parser-relevant functions and symbols in the log include __list_del_entry_valid, __list_add_valid, nf_tables_newflowtable, nfnetlink_rcv_batch, netlink_sendmsg. Diagnostic tokens visible in the complete fixture include kernel panic, page fault/NULL dereference, expected corrupted, expected panicked.

Control flow: the test harness enumerates `pkg/report/testdata/linux/report`, reads expectation headers until the blank line or `REPORT:` marker, and feeds the remaining bytes to a Linux `Reporter`. For this fixture, `ContainsCrash` must match the expected crash, `Parse` must locate the first report span, and `ParseFrom` must rediscover the same crash from its start offset but not after its end offset. The log-specific flow is: multiple page faults at __list_del_entry_valid and __list_add_valid after nf_tables_newflowtable/nfnetlink_rcv_batch activity; corrupted and panicked flags are set. There are 254 source lines; exact report-body comparison is `no`.

State and persistence behavior: all persistent state lives in this text file: header expectations, alternate titles, crash transcript bytes, and any explicit report body. During tests, state is transient parser output: crash start/end offsets, selected title, alternate titles, crash type, corruption/panic flags, guilty-file hints, and trimmed report bytes. The fixture performs no filesystem, network, device, or kernel mutation; it models those kernel-side events only as immutable input text.

Dependencies and integration points: the fixture integrates with syzkaller's Linux report recognizer, stack-frame skip lists, sanitizer parsers, lockdep/warning/hung-task detectors, panic handling, corruption handling, and report-boundary logic. Product-level consumers are crash deduplication, dashboard grouping, repro triage, maintainers' signal routing, and automated bisection. Because the source lives under `testdata/linux/report`, its filename is intentionally opaque; the headers and transcript are the behavioral contract.

Risks and edge cases: CORRUPTED means the parser should preserve bad-access/corrupted labeling instead of overfitting to nf_tables frames. More generally, regressions can come from overfitting to timestamps, CPU/task prefixes, architecture-specific syscall wrappers, compiler suffixes such as `.cold` or `.constprop`, repeated helper frames, panic-on-warn trailers, allocation/free stacks, or noisy subsystem messages preceding the crash. Reports flagged as corrupted must remain conservative about title specificity, while non-crash logs must not be promoted just because they contain alarming words.

Test signals: a passing parser run returns title `BUG: unable to handle kernel paging request in corrupted`, type `MEMORY_SAFETY_BUG`, alternate titles `bad-access in corrupted`, corrupted `Y`, panicked `Y`, and exact-body comparison `no`. It must keep the meaningful frame named by the expected title when the log provides one, avoid helper-only titles, preserve panic/corruption semantics, and produce stable output across `Parse` and `ParseFrom`.
